decisions.rationale: 'familial adenomatous polyposis' names one specific hereditary disease with no further categorization, so the full string is annotated as a single Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: 'tumorigenesis' refers to a biological process, not a disease, so it is excluded.
'FAP' is the abbreviation defined in 'familial APC (FAP)' and denotes the same specific disease. Abbreviation definitions are annotated as a separate mention used as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions); What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'colorectal adenomas' names a specific neoplastic disease (colorectal adenoma) that is the object of 'develop' and is not a modifier; it is treated as a specific condition rather than a family of diseases.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5

decisions.rationale: 'carcinomas' is a broad category covering a family of multiple specific cancers rather than one defined disease, so it is a Disease Class. Cancer/tumor terms are retained.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class); What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer retained)

decisions.rationale: 'disease' is a very general term and is explicitly excluded.

'polyposis' in 'severe polyposis' is a bare term for a family of conditions characterized by multiple polyps, which can be described as a class of several specific diseases rather than one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class); Examples 11 (grey-area terms)

decisions.rationale: 'polyposis' in 'attenuated polyposis' is a bare term for a family of polyposis conditions, consistent with the preceding 'severe polyposis' decision, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class); Examples 11 (grey-area terms)

decisions.rationale: 'FAP' in 'FAP patients' is the abbreviation of a disease used to modify the noun 'patients', so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers); What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions)

decisions.rationale: 'colorectal tumor' modifies the noun 'growth' in 'colorectal tumor growth', so it is used as a Modifier rather than as a standalone disease mention. Tumor terms are retained.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers); What NOT to Annotate 4 (tumor retained)
